sections.title: Snapshot
sections.content: Snapshot time: 2026-11-19 01:42 UTC. Scope: Daily. Date range: 2026-11-19 through 2026-11-19. Ranking basis: daily GitHub Trending star gains.

sections.title: Headline
sections.content: Agent-oriented development dominates today's strongest signals: PaperOrchestra leads the listed repos, while agent skills, harnesses, and software-facing CLIs account for much of the rest. Research automation and self-hosted developer infrastructure provide notable adjacent themes.

sections.title: google-research/paper-orchestra
sections.description: PaperOrchestra is a multi-agent framework for automated AI research paper writing.
sections.content: A multi-agent pipeline that turns research ideas and experiment logs into LaTeX papers, including literature synthesis and visuals.
sections.why_notable: It leads this snapshot by daily star gain and exemplifies specialized-agent orchestration for research writing.
sections.unique_caveat: The README says the dataset used for paper generation is not included in the repository and will be released separately; model-provider credentials may be needed.

sections.title: affaan-m/ECC
sections.description: The agent harness performance optimization system. Skills, instincts, memory, security, and research-first development for Claude Code, Codex, Opencode, Cursor and beyond.
sections.content: An agent-harness optimization system spanning skills, memory, security, and research-first development across coding agents.
sections.why_notable: Its second-place daily gain underscores demand for reusable agent harnesses and operational tooling.
sections.unique_caveat: The repository is a broad, fast-evolving collection of harness components and integrations rather than a single standalone agent model.

sections.title: mvanhorn/last30days-skill
sections.description: AI agent skill that researches any topic across Reddit, X, YouTube, HN, Polymarket, and the web - then synthesizes a grounded summary
sections.content: An AI-agent research skill that gathers current signals from social, video, news, and web sources into a grounded summary.
sections.why_notable: Strong momentum for cross-platform research synthesis, with engagement signals used to rank source material.
sections.unique_caveat: The README notes that some source integrations require user-provided keys or browser sessions and additional setup.

sections.title: obra/superpowers
sections.description: An agentic skills framework & software development methodology that works.
sections.content: A composable skills framework and software-development methodology for coding agents.
sections.why_notable: The README describes a workflow from requirements and approved design through planning, TDD, and subagent-driven implementation.
sections.unique_caveat: It supplies a methodology and skills for supported coding-agent harnesses; it is not a standalone coding model.

sections.title: sveltejs/svelte
sections.description: web development for the rest of us
sections.content: A JavaScript framework for building web interfaces.
sections.why_notable: A mainstream frontend framework is among the day's strongest non-agent signals.

sections.title: getarcaneapp/arcane
sections.description: Modern Docker Management, Designed for Everyone
sections.content: Modern Docker management designed for general users.
sections.why_notable: It represents continued interest in approachable self-hosted container operations.

sections.title: HKUDS/CLI-Anything
sections.description: "CLI-Anything: Making ALL Software Agent-Native" -- CLI-Hub: https://clianything.cc/
sections.content: A toolkit for making software usable by agents through generated command-line interfaces.
sections.why_notable: Its CLI-Hub and software-specific harnesses push the agent trend beyond coding into interaction with existing applications.
sections.unique_caveat: The README describes a growing collection of software-specific harnesses; coverage depends on available or contributed integrations.

sections.title: google-labs-code/stitch-skills
sections.description: A library of Agent Skills designed to work with the Stitch MCP server. Each skill follows the Agent Skills open standard, for compatibility with coding agents such as Antigravity, Gemini CLI, Claude Code, Cursor.
sections.content: Agent Skills for Google's Stitch MCP server, designed to work across compatible coding agents.
sections.why_notable: It reflects the spread of portable skill packages and MCP-connected design workflows.
sections.unique_caveat: Designed for use with the Stitch MCP server, so its workflow is tied to that service.

sections.title: n8n-io/n8n
sections.description: Fair-code workflow automation platform with native AI capabilities. Combine visual building with custom code, self-host or cloud, 400+ integrations.
sections.content: A fair-code workflow automation platform with AI capabilities, integrations, and self-hosted or cloud operation.
sections.why_notable: It shows sustained pull for visual automation that can combine AI and conventional integrations.
sections.unique_caveat: The project uses a fair-code license rather than an OSI-approved open-source license.

sections.title: cursor/plugins
sections.description: Cursor plugin specification and official plugins
sections.content: The Cursor plugin specification and official plugins.
sections.why_notable: Another concrete ecosystem signal for packaging agent and editor capabilities as installable plugins.
sections.unique_caveat: The repository represents Cursor's plugin ecosystem and specification, not a standalone editor or general-purpose plugin standard.

sections.title: Trending Technologies and Themes
sections.content: Agent workflows and reusable capabilities: PaperOrchestra, ECC, Superpowers, Stitch Skills, and Cursor Plugins show interest in multi-agent pipelines, harnesses, shared skills, and plugin ecosystems. Agents across software and information sources: CLI-Anything targets software interfaces, while last30days-skill unifies research across platforms. Self-hosted and visual automation: Arcane and n8n. Languages: Python and TypeScript lead with three listed repositories each; JavaScript appears twice, while Go and Shell appear once each.

sections.title: Takeaway
sections.content: Today's snapshot points to an ecosystem shift from standalone coding assistants toward the surrounding systems: reusable skills, agent harnesses, multi-agent workflows, and interfaces that let agents act on existing tools. Traditional frontend and automation projects still attract meaningful daily interest, but the clearest concentration is in making agents more capable and deployable.
